description: Deliberate, reviewed departures from policy. An exception is not a suppression: each one states what is being departed from, why it is correct here, and what would make it worth revisiting. An exception with no review trigger is a permanent hole and should be a policy change instead.

exceptions.statement: The Taskiq worker and scheduler services have healthchecks explicitly disabled, while every other long-running service has one.
exceptions.reason: Neither process serves a port or exposes a readiness surface, so any healthcheck would either be a process-liveness tautology or a false signal. Disabling it explicitly is more honest than an inherited check that always passes. Their failure mode is a queue that stops draining, which is observable from Redis rather than from the container.
exceptions.review_trigger: A queue stall goes unnoticed in an environment where nobody is watching Redis.

exceptions.statement: The MCP sidecars, the browser service, pgweb, and Traefik declare no healthcheck.
exceptions.reason: Healthchecks exist here to make `depends_on: service_healthy` meaningful. Nothing waits on readiness for any of these: the MCP sidecars are probed by the application at connection time and skipped when unreachable, chrome-devtools-mcp waits on browserless only for service_started, and pgweb and Traefik are entered by a human rather than by another service. Adding a healthcheck to each would be ceremony that proves a process is running, which is what the container runtime already reports.
scope: docker-compose.yml services browserless, chrome-devtools-mcp, docling-mcp, github-mcp, pgweb
exceptions.review_trigger: Any service starts depending on one of these being healthy, or an MCP sidecar failure stops being invisible to the application's probe-and-skip path.

exceptions.statement: The Trivy image scan in CI runs with exit-code 0 and can never fail the build.
exceptions.reason: The scan reports CRITICAL and HIGH findings in base images that are pinned by digest and cannot always be fixed on the repository's schedule. Blocking on it before the finding volume is known would train people to bypass CI. Recorded as deliberate rather than left looking like an oversight, and used as the pilot for the advisory-to-blocking promotion ladder.
exceptions.review_trigger: Promotion criteria in the trivy-image-scan rule are met, or a vulnerability ships that the scan reported and nobody read.

exceptions.statement: Migration filenames are not contiguously numbered: 0017 and 0019 through 0021 do not exist, and 0004_5 is interleaved.
exceptions.reason: Filename numbering is not the contiguity signal — the revision graph is. The chain is linear and unbroken from 0000_users to 0027_embedding_cache; the gaps are history, from revisions that were written and dropped before release. A policy keyed to filenames would fire on day one and be disabled by day two.
exceptions.review_trigger: The revision graph itself becomes disconnected or grows an unexpected head.

exceptions.statement: Migrations create organization, plan, subscription, seat, Stripe event, and credits-usage tables that no ORM model, service, or route uses.
exceptions.reason: The project was generated with billing disabled. The schema shipped anyway, so these tables are expected-present-unused rather than orphans. Classifying them from the generator context means orphan detection can tell 'never wired up' apart from 'wired up and then abandoned', which are very different problems.
scope: database tables: organizations, plans, plan_prices, subscriptions, billing_seats, stripe_events, credits_usage, mv_usage_daily
exceptions.review_trigger: Billing is enabled, or the generator drops the schema for disabled features.

exceptions.statement: The chat WebSocket connects from the browser to the backend origin directly, bypassing the Next.js proxy layer that every REST call goes through.
exceptions.reason: Proxying a long-lived streaming socket through the Next.js server would add a hop that buys nothing and costs connection stability and backpressure fidelity. The access token travels as a WebSocket subprotocol rather than a query parameter, so it stays out of access logs and Referer headers. This is the single exception, and it is modelled explicitly so impact analysis knows the proxy hop is absent here rather than missing.
exceptions.review_trigger: A second direct browser-to-backend edge is proposed, at which point this stops being an exception and becomes a pattern needing a policy.

exceptions.statement: The live Google Workspace test suite is absent from the validator registry rather than present and marked destructive.
exceptions.reason: It sends real email and mutates a live account. Being absent is the enforcement: impact analysis, agents, and CI select validators by ID from the registry, so a suite that is not in it cannot be selected by any path. Marking it present-but-destructive would leave a name that some future selection logic could still resolve. It is recorded in the registry's excluded list so the omission reads as deliberate.
exceptions.review_trigger: A caller needs to run it programmatically, which would mean designing a safe harness first.

exceptions.statement: The Playwright end-to-end suite runs locally only and is not part of any CI job.
exceptions.reason: Its webServer is disabled under CI and the tests need a running backend, so as shipped the CI step could only ever fail or vacuously pass. Removing it was more honest than leaving a step that never proved anything. E2E remains available as make playwright against a local stack.
exceptions.review_trigger: A composed CI stack exists that can bring up the backend, at which point the suite should return to CI.

exceptions.statement: The settings/account page POSTs /api/auth/password/change and the admin/system page GETs /api/health/ready; neither endpoint exists yet, and both pages handle the failure gracefully by design.
exceptions.reason: Both calls are documented wishlist surface rather than regressions: the account page catches the failure and tells the user password change requires backend wiring, and the system page probes /health/ready with a catch-to-null and labels it a backend wishlist item in its own UI copy. Counting them as broken chains on every sweep buries real breaks; recording them as accepted keeps the rule's signal clean while the wish stays visible here.
exceptions.review_trigger: The backend lands a password-change endpoint or a per-service /health/ready; wire the page for real and retire this exception.

exceptions.statement: The five preflight validators (preflight-volumes, preflight-model, preflight-ports, preflight-edge-ports, preflight-mcp) declare ci_job null and run in no CI job.
exceptions.reason: Each one probes the developer's host rather than the repository: the external preservation volumes and Docker Model Runner exist only on a machine that runs the stack, free host ports mean nothing on an ephemeral runner, and the MCP token check would have to be fed dummy values to pass, proving nothing. They are also PowerShell-only by design. Running them in CI would be a step that always fails or always vacuously passes, which is the condition the playwright-not-in-ci exception was written to avoid.
scope: governance/validators.json entries preflight-volumes, preflight-model, preflight-ports, preflight-edge-ports, preflight-mcp
exceptions.review_trigger: A self-hosted runner with a Docker engine and Docker Model Runner joins the pipeline, at which point preflight-volumes and preflight-model become meaningful there.

exceptions.statement: Coverage thresholds are set at measured levels — 54 percent on the backend and single digits to seventeen percent on the frontend — rather than at an aspirational target.
exceptions.reason: The generator shipped 100 percent thresholds against roughly 55 percent and 4 percent actuals, so the gate had never passed and every CI run failed on it. A floor at the measured level catches regressions immediately, which is what a gate is for. It is a ratchet: raise it when real tests are added, never lower it to make a red build green.
exceptions.review_trigger: A meaningful body of tests lands without the floor moving, which means the ratchet is not being maintained.
